questions.question: A Multinational Corporation (MNC) is defined as a company that:
options: Operates exclusively within a single municipal district
Is owned and directed by the United Nations General Assembly
Produces goods exclusively for non-profit charitable donation
Owns or controls production of goods and services in more than one nation
questions.explanation: A Multinational Corporation (MNC) is a company that owns or controls production in more than one nation. MNCs set up offices and factories for production in regions where they can get cheap labour and other resources.

questions.subtopic: Why MNCs Set Up Production Globally
questions.question: Why do MNCs locate their production units in different countries across the globe?
options: To minimise the cost of production and maximise their profits by leveraging cheap labour, resources, and proximity to markets
To distribute 100% of their revenues as free aid to foreign citizens
Because their home countries have legally banned all factory manufacturing
To avoid communicating with international transport companies
questions.explanation: MNCs set up production where it is close to the markets; where there is skilled and unskilled labour available at low costs; and where the availability of other factors of production is assured. This is done so that the cost of production is low and the MNCs can earn greater profits.

options: It prevents domestic producers from selling products within their home towns
It mandates that all goods must be gifted to foreign consumers for free
It forces manufacturers to convert factories into agricultural fields
It allows producers to reach beyond domestic borders and compete in international global markets

Producers can sell their produce not only in markets located within the country but can also compete in markets located in other countries of the world.

questions.question: Why did the Indian government put strict trade barriers on foreign imports following Independence in 1947?

Because international shipping ports did not exist in India before 1991
Because the United Nations ordered India to ban foreign commerce
To protect newly emerging domestic industries from foreign competition during their nascent infant stage
questions.explanation: The Indian government, after Independence, had put barriers to foreign trade and foreign investment. This was considered necessary to protect the producers within the country from foreign competition. Industries were just coming up in the 1950s and 1960s, and competition from imports at that stage would not have allowed these industries to survive.

questions.question: What is the primary stated objective of the World Trade Organisation (WTO)?
options: To enforce a universal currency across all seven continents
To liberalise international trade and oversee that multilateral trade rules are obeyed by member nations
To command military peacekeeping troops in conflict zones

Ravi was appointed chief director of the World Trade Organisation
Ravi's factory output expanded by 1,000% within two months
